pr_title: Remove references to EVP_sha1() and EVP_sha256()
pr_body:
There are a few remaining references.  These take two forms:

1. legacy APIs that don't know to free the EVP_MD after they finish using it
2. APIs that only use the name or NID of the EVP_MD

Fixes #14387

- [ ] documentation is added or updated
- [ ] tests are added or updated
pr_comments: I am never sure if any of the fetches need the fallback path for engines...

Ones that obviously might, I didn't change.  Those with a libctx and properties are most likely safe.  The ones I'd be concerned about are the ones that subtly might depend -- these we can revert as they are bought up.
This pull request is ready to merge

issue_context.title: Equality tests on EVP_sha1() etc should not be called
issue_context.body:
In a number of places in the code we have

`if (md == EVP_sha1())`

and that is something we should not be doing. If we want to know if something is SHA1 then testing this way is simply not the right way to do it. It will break in unexpected ways.

```
./ts/ts_rsp_sign.c:        || ctx->ess_cert_id_digest == EVP_sha1()) {
./x509/x_all.c:    if (type == EVP_sha1() && (data->flags & EXFLAG_SET) != 0
./cms/cms_sd.c:            if (md == EVP_sha1() || md == NULL) {
```
comments:
Should be replaced with EVP_MD_is_a
also
```
; g grep '== EVP_md'  
crypto/ec/ecx_meth.c:        if (p2 == NULL || (const EVP_MD *)p2 == EVP_md_null())
; g grep --extended '[!=]= EVP_[a-zA-Z0-9]+\('
# duplicates removed 
crypto/ess/ess_lib.c:    if (hash_alg != EVP_sha256()) {
```
Shane already did a PR #14474 that addressed most of these.  All of the == tests and a number of others.

What's left are in his comment: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/14474#issuecomment-817429336

> There are still some calls to EVP_Digest() and EVP_DigestInit_ex()
> If you do a search for EVP_sha1()
> EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_dh_kdf_md() also
>
> Note that X509_digest() is fine since it uses the libctx from the cert.

Including a few EVP_sha256() references, the relevant file list is:
```
crypto/asn1/x_algor.c
crypto/rsa/rsa_oaep.c
crypto/rsa/rsa_pmeth.c
crypto/pem/pvkfmt.c
crypto/ocsp/ocsp_lib.c
crypto/ocsp/ocsp_vfy.c
crypto/evp/p5_crpt2.c
crypto/cms/cms_dh.c
crypto/cms/cms_smime.c
crypto/cms/cms_ec.c
crypto/x509/v3_skid.c
crypto/x509/v3_purp.c
crypto/x509/t_x509.c
crypto/x509/x_crl.c
crypto/ess/ess_lib.c
crypto/srp/srp_vfy.c
crypto/pkcs12/p12_crt.c
crypto/pkcs12/p12_mutl.c
```

plus _crypto/evp/dh_ctrl.c_ that defines `EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_dh_kdf_md()`.

review_comments: another case where we have multiple things with no libctx.. (and RAND_priv_bytes)
`RAND_priv_bytes` doesn't need a libctx, the DRBGs are created once and then it is per thread.

The point being that there are not too many instances of  RAND_priv_bytes() left..
i.e RAND_priv_bytes_ex() is used in most places.
SRP interfaces are deprecated and we should not add _ex() calls to them.
Hmmmm, no comment about the `EVP_MD_fetch(NULL, ..., NULL)` two lines down :laughing:  I can't see anywhere to extract a libctx from, so I'm with @t8m, live and let die.

Is this method legacy only? (i.e no libctx)
I've no idea :(
It's guarded by a `#ifndef OPENSSL_NO_RC4`.  I'm not seeing a compelling need to introduce an _ex flavour.
Moreover, none of its callers have access to a libctx.

It could be pulled out as a standalone KDF I guess.  I'm not seeing much value to doing so.
